topic: Your boat sinks and you are alone in a life raft. How long can a person last?
title: Alone In A Life Raft
idea: One sailor lasted seventy six days; in a raft, survival is about saving the body water you have and staying findable.
hook: Your boat is gone, and you're alone in a raft.

beats.line: One sailor lived through exactly this, so guess how many days he lasted.
beats.see: Wide ocean, tiny orange raft bobbing; a big guess counter '? DAYS' drops in at the top with a ticking dial. Raft bobs on 'sailor', counter on 'guess'.

beats.line: Seventy six days, in a raft about six feet long.
beats.see: Counter spins and slams to 76 with a stamp DAYS; a measuring tape unrolls along the raft reading 6 FT, the sailor curled up inside. Stamp on 'Seventy six', tape on 'six feet'.

beats.line: He distilled drinking water and caught fish.
beats.see: Close-up in the raft: a clear dome still with droplets running into a cup, then a fish flips up out of the water into his hands. Drops on 'water', fish jumps on 'fish'.

beats.line: Survival trainers say every drop of body water you save buys you time.
beats.see: Cutaway body with a blue water gauge in the torso; each saved droplet adds a tick to a clock beside it. Gauge glows on 'body water', clock ticks on 'time'.

beats.line: So put up the canopy, save your energy, and ration your sweat.
beats.see: Step card SHADE: the raft canopy pops up and a shadow falls over the sailor, the sun icon bounces off; he lies still and sweat drops above his head shrink to one. Canopy on 'canopy', drops shrink on 'sweat'.

beats.line: Stream the sea anchor to stay near your last reported position.
beats.see: Top down map: a dashed drift line starts racing away from a red X marked LAST POSITION; a small cone anchor splashes out on a rope and the drift line slows and curls near the X. Anchor splash on 'anchor', line slows on 'stay near'.

beats.line: Switch on your emergency beacon and leave it on.
beats.see: Step card BEACON: a yellow beacon on the raft edge flicks on, radio rings pulse upward to a satellite icon and keep pulsing. Light on 'Switch', rings on 'leave it on'.

beats.line: Keep flashing a mirror at the horizon.
beats.see: Step card MIRROR: he holds a small mirror up, a white flash beam sweeps across the horizon and glints on a distant ship silhouette. Flash on 'flashing', glint on 'horizon'.

end.line: Seventy six days, and it started just like this, alone in a raft.
end.see: Pull back to the same wide ocean and tiny orange raft as the hook; the 76 DAYS stamp fades in small above it, then out. Stamp on 'Seventy six', raft alone on 'raft', last frame = hook frame.

description: Your boat is gone and you're alone in a life raft. One sailor survived for a long time like this. Guess how many days.

facts.claim: Solo sailor Steven Callahan survived 76 days in a 6-foot (1.8 m) life raft by snagging fish and distilling water.
His boat sank on 4 February 1982 and he was found by three fishermen in the Caribbean.
Every bit of body water you conserve will increase the length of your survival; ration your sweat and save your energy; put up the canopy.
Stream the sea anchor: it reduces your drift rate, helping to keep you near your last reported position.
Turn on the EPIRB and leave it on until rescued; sweep the horizon often with your mirror's signal.

notes: Guess number = seventy six days (Callahan). Deliberately says nothing about seawater or urine (covered in 030; AMSEA says never drink either if a viewer asks). 'Distilled drinking water' follows National Geographic's 'distilling water'; do not label the device 'solar still' on screen. 'Survival trainers' = AMSEA (marine safety education group). The ship on the horizon in the mirror beat is a target, not a claim; do not show a ship count (sources disagree, seven vs nine). Do not imply Callahan's beacon saved him (it did not). Big number: seventy six days.
